Nasdaq was weak over the same days (QQQ 688 to 652 since 11-12), with hawkish Fed commentary cited.
view: I could not find a WeRide-specific datum from the quarter that the price does not already hold. The company's news flow since the Q2 call is thin: the Spain permit, the HKEX Tech 100 inclusion, an insurance program and an AION i60 L2++ launch. I found no new fleet counts, no fresh Middle East driverless milestones, no pre-announcement and no dated analyst revisions. The reaction will most likely turn on Q3 revenue and robotaxi growth against a thin RMB 270M consensus, on cash burn (cash fell from about RMB 7.1B to 5.4B in H1, buyback and capex included) and on any 2026-27 fleet target. Two structural forces point opposite ways. First, the stock has been liquidated into the print, falling 21% in five sessions to an all-time low with no company news I could find. Combined with a moderate short base and an EV of only about $360M, that sets up a relief bounce on an in-line or better quarter. Second, the closest analogue, Pony two days ago, shows the tape is selling robotaxi beats: a clear revenue beat gave an 11% pre-market pop that had reversed to about -5% by midday, which is exactly the window scored here (exit 13:00 ET). WeRide's own Q2 print in August was also sold (-9.6%) despite +82% revenue. And Q2's product revenue spike makes a QoQ step-up to RMB 270M less than assured. Neither force is a dated, checkable mechanism. I sit near a coin flip with a very slight lean down, and the expected size is large in either direction.

recommendation.reason: I found no dated evidence about the quarter that the price lacks. The two setups I can see work against each other and neither can be shown: oversold into the print with a thin EV, against a sector tape that sold Pony's beat inside the same intraday window. A 53% lean is not a bet.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Revenue well above RMB 270M with a quantified 2027 fleet or Middle East driverless target and a smaller cash burn would make the oversold bounce the likelier path. A product-revenue-driven miss would make the Pony fade the floor case.

self_critique: The case against a slight lean down is the setup itself. The stock was liquidated 21% in five days with no company news, trades at about 1.3x cash, and carries a rising short base, so even an in-line quarter with steady cash burn could produce a sharp relief rally, as the +14.7% on the Q3 2025 print did. Pony's fade happened after a pre-print run-up in its HK line, which differs from WeRide's straight-down pre-print path. The case against any lean at all: one peer analogue and one prior reaction are anecdotes, not a base rate.
approach_notes: P4 and P6 helped: the peer's intraday path inside the same scoring window was the most informative thing I found. P3's fresh-data search turned up little for a Chinese AV issuer with thin English coverage and quiet IR, and the playbook gives no guidance on weighing an oversold pre-print setup against a peer's beat-and-fade.
